• Consolidated Revenue: Increased 20.8% YoY to ₹4,870 Cr, up 5% QoQ.

• Consolidated EBITDA: Rose 8.8% YoY to ₹778 Cr, with margin at 16% versus 17.7% YoY.

• Standalone Revenue: Grew 29.8% YoY to ₹2,526.4 Cr, supported by strong domestic and export demand.

• Standalone EBITDA: Increased 20.2% YoY to ₹654.6 Cr, with margin at 25.9%.

• FY27 Growth Guidance: Management maintains 20–25% revenue growth expectations for Indian manufacturing.

• Defence Order Book: Strong outstanding order book of ₹10,960 Cr as of H1 FY27.

• New Orders: Secured ₹2,107 Cr during H1 FY27, including ₹681 Cr from Defence.

• ATAGS Programme: Received Bulk Production Clearance; manufacturing to begin in FY27, with revenue recognition from Q1 FY28.

• Capex Expansion: ₹2,000+ Cr investment across Automotive, Aerospace, Defence, Energetics, Data Centres and Semiconductor components, with facilities coming online over 12–18 months.

• Export Performance: Revenue surged 38.9% YoY to ₹1,308.8 Cr, driven by commercial vehicles (+96.2%) and passenger vehicles (+20%).

• Domestic Business: Revenue increased 19.3% YoY, supported by commercial vehicles (+43.9%) and passenger vehicles (+32%).

• Overseas Operations: EBITDA declined to ₹22.3 Cr from ₹48.1 Cr YoY; management undertaking a strategic review amid weak profitability.

• Management Outlook: Expects major capacity-led growth from FY29, supported by defence execution, aerospace expansion and high-value manufacturing diversification.

• OpenAI Revenue: Annualised revenue run rate estimated at $50 Bn in September 2026, growing approximately 77% YoY

• Oracle Opportunity: Potential $300 Bn contract opportunity, with only 57% of modelled OpenAI contract revenue expected to be recognised through Oracle FY30

• CoreWeave: Existing contracts offer revenue visibility, but renewal pricing could face pressure as compute capacity expands

• GPU Oversupply Risk: Bernstein sees potential supply-demand normalisation within 2–3 years, potentially pressuring GPU rental rates

• Infrastructure Economics: Rising AI demand may not translate into equally strong profitability across all data centre operators

• Competitive Advantage: Customer relationships, integrated software platforms and pricing power could become increasingly important

• Hardware Cycle: NVIDIA, AMD and memory suppliers remain exposed to AI infrastructure investment trends, while future returns depend on demand, pricing and capacity utilisation

• Investment Outlook: AI infrastructure spending could continue expanding even as returns weaken for undifferentiated compute providers

• Election Concerns: Democratic victories in Texas and Georgia have raised investor concerns over tighter data centre permitting and construction delays. 

• Texas Restrictions: Data centre permitting restrictions were already in place before the elections, with grid and environmental reviews delaying approvals

• New York Restrictions: State introduced a one-year pause on certain new hyperscale data centre permits in July 2026. 

• 2027 Capacity Outlook: Of approximately 40 GW of proposed US capacity, the analysis estimates only 25–30 GW may become operational due to permitting, equipment and construction constraints.

• 2028 Capacity Outlook: Of approximately 60 GW planned, the analysis expects 35–40 GW to be completed.

• AI Demand: Slower data centre construction does not necessarily reduce demand for AI computing infrastructure.

• GPU Rental Prices: The analysis reports NVIDIA H100 rental rates rising approximately 35% since January, while B200 rental rates increased 11% in the past month.

• Existing GPU Assets: Limited new compute supply could support higher rental rates and extend the economic life of older GPUs.

• Hardware Spending: Project delays could spread AI infrastructure investments over several years, potentially extending the hardware investment cycle.

• Key Risks: Power availability, permitting restrictions, project economics, financing and construction delays remain major challenges.

• Market Outlook: The analysis argues that recent weakness in AI hardware stocks may be excessive, although earnings risks and the extent of project delays remain uncertain.

Alembic Pharmaceuticals Ltd – STRATEGIC COLLABORATION EXPANSION WITH DIFGEN

Expansion of collaboration with DifGen Pharmaceuticals to grow complex generics portfolio in the US:

- Portfolio includes 20+ differentiated products across injectable, transdermal, ophthalmic, and oral dosage forms

- Aggregate reference market for the portfolio is approximately US$5 billion

- Initial product launches are expected from FY28

- Collaboration combines DifGen’s US manufacturing with Alembic’s US commercial platform

- Includes access to DifGen’s US manufacturing facilities for select dosage forms

**Arvind Fashions

A few interesting commitments:

→ Mid-double-digit revenue growth for the balance of FY27
→ 30–40 bps EBITDA margin expansion
→ D2C share target of ~65%, from 53% currently
→ H2 free cash flow release of ₹150–175 crore, with a large part intended for debt reduction.
Growth, channel mix and balance-sheet improvement. Worth tracking together.**

**Carborundum Universal Q2

A good example of why segment-level analysis matters.

FY27 guidance:

→ Ceramics growth raised to 25–28%
→ Ceramics margin raised to 22.5–23.5%
→ Abrasives margin lowered to 8–8.5%.
Different segments, different trajectories. Consolidated numbers may not tell the complete story.**

**Tanfac Industries Q2

Management raised FY27 revenue growth guidance from 30% to 35–40%.

The bigger story is HFC-32:

→ 2,000–3,000 tonnes volume ramp-up in FY27
→ ~95% utilisation targeted in FY28
→ FY28 EBITDA margin guidance: 24–26%.
A significant capacity ramp-up lies ahead.**

**Dhoot Transmission Q2 

Strong growth ambitions:

→ FY27 revenue growth: 40–45%
→ FY27 capex: ~₹750 crore
→ EBITDA margin: 15–16%
→ Three additional wiring harness plants expected by mid-FY28.
Now, execution and utilisation will be key to watch.**

**GNG Electronics

Management raised its FY27 revenue growth guidance to ~40%.
PAT margin expansion guidance also improved from 100 bps to 150 bps over FY26.
One thing to watch: inventory is expected to remain elevated through Q4 FY27.**

**PRABHUDAS LILLADHER – INDRAPRASTHA GAS (IGL)**

**Rating & Target Price**
- Rating: Buy.
- Target price revised to ₹161 from ₹165.

**Q2 FY27 Performance**
- EBITDA loss: ₹30 Cr.
- EBITDA missed estimates significantly.
- EBITDA/scm: -₹0.30 vs ₹3.40 in Q1.
- Gas costs increased 22% QoQ, 47.9% YoY.

**Volume Performance**
- Total volumes: 10.1 mmscmd, up 8% YoY.
- CNG volumes: 7.6 mmscmd, up 8.7%.
- PNG volumes: 2.5 mmscmd, up 6%.
- Total volumes grew 4.2% QoQ.

**Margin & Supply Outlook**
- Spot LNG share increased to 15% from 3%.
- Management retains ₹6–7/scm EBITDA guidance.
- Term LNG supplies expected from Q3.
- Further supply additions expected during Q4.
- Targets approximately 10% volume growth.

**Valuation**
- Standalone business valued at 10x Sep'28E EPS.
- Investments valued at ₹21/share.
- Holding company discount: 25%.

**Key Takeaway**
- Higher spot gas costs severely impacted margins.
- Strong volume growth remains encouraging.
- Term LNG recovery is the key catalyst.
- Impact: **Mixed to Positive**

**KOTAK INSTITUTIONAL EQUITIES – SBI**

**Rating & Target Price**
- Rating: Buy.
- Target price: ₹1,250.

**Q2 FY27 Performance**
- Earnings growth: 15% YoY.
- Operating profit growth: 7% YoY.
- Mutual fund stake-sale gain supported earnings.
- NII growth: Around 15% YoY.
- NIM recovered approximately 10bps QoQ.
- Credit cost remained low at 30bps.
- RoE stood at 15%.

**Asset Quality & Valuation**
- Asset quality remains a minor concern.
- Attractive valuation supports investment appeal.
- Strong franchise offers superior return potential.

**Key Takeaway**
- Healthy NII growth supports profitability.
- Low credit costs strengthen return profile.
- Attractive valuation supports positive outlook.
- Impact: **Positive**

**NOMURA – STATE BANK OF INDIA (SBI)**

**Rating & Target Price**
- Rating: Neutral.
- Target price: ₹1,100.

**Q2 FY27 Performance**
- NII exceeded estimates on NIM expansion.
- Core performance remained broadly in line.
- Slower loan growth remained a concern.
- Higher opex impacted profitability.
- Weak treasury performance added pressure.
- SBI Funds stake-sale gain supported earnings.
- Higher opex and lower other income hurt PPOP.

**Growth & Asset Quality**
- FY27 loan growth guidance retained at 14–15%.
- Asset quality remained benign.

**Key Takeaway**
- NIM expansion supported NII outperformance.
- One-time gains supported reported earnings.
- Slower growth and higher costs remain concerns.
- Impact: **Neutral**

**CITI – STATE BANK OF INDIA (SBI)**

**Rating & Target Price**
- Rating: Buy.
- Target price: ₹1,300.

**Q2 FY27 Financial Performance**
- PAT: ₹23,000 Cr, up 14% YoY.
- Stake-sale gain: ₹7,290 Cr.
- Treasury loss: ₹1,280 Cr.
- Operating expenses rose 15% YoY, 38% QoQ.
- NII grew 14% YoY, 4.6% QoQ.
- NII exceeded estimates.
- NIM expanded 8bps QoQ.
- Estimates had projected a 2bps decline.

**NIM & Loan Growth Outlook**
- 49% of loans linked to external benchmarks.
- 32% of loans are repo-linked.
- Rising rates could support NIMs.
- Management retained 3%+ NIM guidance.
- Loan growth: 18.2% YoY, 3.3% QoQ.
- Corporate lending remained flat.
- FY27 advances guidance: 14–15%.
- Citi expects loan growth above 16%.

**Asset Quality & ECL**
- Slippages remained below 0.5%.
- Credit costs remained below 0.35%.
- ECL transition impact: ₹19,500 Cr.
- Equivalent to 3.3% of net worth.
- Equivalent to 0.4% of advances.

**Key Takeaway**
- Strong NII and NIM recovery support earnings.
- Stake-sale gains boosted reported PAT.
- Loan growth remains a key monitorable.
- Asset quality remains healthy.
- Impact: **Positive**

**HSBC – STATE BANK OF INDIA (SBI)**

**Rating & Target Price**
- Rating: Buy.
- Target price: ₹1,220.

**Q2 FY27 Review**
- Strong NII and NIM performance.
- Loan growth remained relatively lower.
- Operating expenses exceeded estimates.

**Earnings Estimates & Valuation**
- FY27–29E EPS estimates upgraded 4–8%.
- Stronger NIM momentum supports earnings upgrades.
- Operating leverage expected to support profitability.
- Target price reduced despite EPS upgrades.
- Lower target multiples for subsidiaries.
- Valuation factors in slower loan growth.

**Key Takeaway**
- Strong NIM momentum supports earnings outlook.
- Operating leverage provides additional earnings support.
- Slower loan growth limits valuation upside.
- Impact: **Positive**

**BERNSTEIN – STATE BANK OF INDIA (SBI)**

**Rating & Target Price**
- Rating: Market Perform.
- Target price: ₹1,300.

**Q2 FY27 Performance**
- Headline earnings supported by lower credit costs.
- Stake-sale gains boosted reported profitability.
- Loan growth remained healthy.
- NIM improved 8bps QoQ.
- Underlying PPOP declined 1% YoY.
- Lower other income and higher expenses impacted PPOP.

**Underlying Profitability**
- Adjusted EPS growth: 5% YoY.
- Reported EPS growth: 13% YoY.
- Adjusted RoA declined 21bps QoQ to 0.90%.
- Reported RoA stood at 1.19%.

**Key Takeaway**
- Headline earnings masked softer underlying performance.
- NIM recovery failed to improve core profitability.
- Higher expenses remain a key concern.
- Impact: **Neutral**

**CLSA – STATE BANK OF INDIA (SBI)**

**Rating & Target Price**
- Rating: Outperform.
- Target price: ₹1,325.

**Q2 FY27 Performance**
- NII beat estimates by 2%.
- Domestic NIM expanded 11bps QoQ.
- PBT missed estimates by 3%.
- Lower fee income and treasury losses impacted PBT.

**Loan & Deposit Growth**
- Domestic loan growth: 17% YoY.
- Growth remained broad-based.
- International loans declined 3% QoQ.
- Deposit growth: 12% YoY.
- CASA growth: 8% YoY.

**Asset Quality**
- Asset quality continued improving.
- Net slippages declined 10bps YoY.

**Regulatory Impact**
- New insurance distribution rules expected limited impact.
- Distribution income contributes below 3% of PBT.

**Key Takeaway**
- Strong NII growth supported by NIM expansion.
- Broad-based domestic loan growth remains healthy.
- Improving asset quality supports earnings visibility.
- Impact: **Positive**

**Rating & Target Price**
- Rating: Outperform.

- Exceptional gains supported reported earnings.
- Loan growth remained healthy.
- Margins remained resilient.
- Asset quality remained healthy.
- Expected ECL impact remains manageable.

- RoA guidance: 1%.
- Domestic NIM guidance: Above 3%.

**Key Takeaway**
- Strong NII and NIM supported quarterly performance.
- Higher expenses and slower loan growth remain concerns.
- Listing gain boosted reported profitability.
- Impact: **Mixed**

**GOLDMAN SACHS – NEULAND LABORATORIES**

**Rating & Target Price**
- Rating: Buy.
- Target price: ₹25,275.

**Q2 FY27 Performance**
- Sales declined 13% YoY.
- EBITDA declined 37% YoY.
- Performance exceeded Goldman Sachs estimates.
- Commercial CMS was 5% below estimates.
- Spec API segment was 21% below estimates.
- EBITDA margin: 21.7%, down 856bps YoY.
- Operating deleverage impacted margins.

**Business Outlook & Growth Drivers**
- Commercial CMS scale-up expected in FY27–28.
- At least two new late-stage projects.
- Pipeline includes peptide opportunities.
- Sterile API collaboration with Gland Pharma.
- Expanding peptides and complex molecule capabilities.
- Capacity expansion supports future growth.

**Management Guidance**
- Medium-term growth aspiration: Around 20%.
- Quarterly performance may remain uneven.
- CMS ordering patterns remain inherently lumpy.

**Key Takeaway**
- Weak Q2 profitability reflects operating deleverage.
- CMS scale-up remains the key growth driver.
- New pipeline supports medium-term growth visibility.
- Impact: **Mixed**

- Revenue growth remains modest.
- Profitability significantly missed expectations.
- Citi sees further valuation downside risk.
- Impact: **Negative**

While platforms enforce tighter community standards, users face lengthy grievance-redressal delays, making it increasingly difficult to challenge blocked accounts and secure timely relief.

Curious when FII will come back to India

So gave Co-pilot a prompt
“Why FIIs wont return to India even as AI trade unwind globally”

Reverse Psychology

Here is the response

1. India is still expensive vs EM peers
o Even after corrections, India trades at a premium to most emerging markets.
o FIIs compare India with China, Korea, Taiwan, Brazil, not with India's own history.
o If China is at 10-12x PE and India at 20-25x PE, capital tends to chase cheaper markets. 
2. India lacks direct AI beneficiaries
o The AI trade created winners in US tech, Taiwan semiconductors and Korean memory-chip companies.
o India has very few large listed AI, semiconductor or hyperscaler plays that global thematic funds can buy. 
3. Dollar returns matter, not rupee returns
o FIIs think in USD.
o Even if Nifty is flat or slightly up, rupee depreciation can wipe out returns.
o Currency risk remains a major deterrent for foreign capital. 
4. US yields remain a strong competitor
o If US Treasuries offer attractive risk-free returns, FIIs need a much higher expected return from India.
o Many global allocators prefer earning 4-5% in dollar assets rather than taking EM risk. 
5. India's earnings growth has moderated
o India's premium valuation was justified when earnings were compounding rapidly.
o If earnings growth slows while valuations remain rich, FIIs question the risk-reward. 
6. Better opportunities elsewhere
o Korea, Taiwan and China offer exposure to AI, semiconductors and manufacturing at lower valuations.
o Global funds have finite capital; India is competing against these markets for allocation. 
7. India is no longer an under-owned market
o After years of strong inflows, most EM funds already have meaningful India exposure.
o Incremental flows require a new catalyst, not just the absence of AI enthusiasm.
8. Domestic flows reduce urgency
o SIPs, mutual funds and insurance money continue supporting Indian markets despite FII selling.
o Paradoxically, this resilience prevents large valuation corrections that would otherwise attract FIIs back.

Maruti Suzuki India should be rechristened as Suzuki India

Maruti's journey started as a Govt of India project. Maruti Udyog was the Indian promoter & Suzuki was brought in as the technology partner. Back then, this was very much an Indian company with Japanese know-how.

Over time, the Indian promoter gradually diluted its holding & eventually exited completely. Suzuki did the opposite, staying invested through every cycle & steadily increasing its stake.

What began as a JV slowly became Suzuki's most important global asset. The ownership story itself tells you who has deepened commitment over the decades.

For years, investors debated why Suzuki was setting up fresh manufacturing capacity outside Maruti Suzuki through its Gujarat subsidiary instead of housing it directly in the listed entity.

Then came the reversal. Suzuki transferred Suzuki Motor Gujarat into Maruti Suzuki at a valuation of roughly ₹12,000+ Cr. Rather than taking cash, it largely took equity.

The result? Suzuki's ownership in Maruti Suzuki moved up further without having to buy equivalent shares from the secondary market.

This wasn't just a restructuring exercise. It was Suzuki effectively converting manufacturing assets into a larger stake in India's largest PV company.

Even after that transaction, Suzuki did not stop. It has periodically picked up additional shares from the open market whenever opportunities emerged.

The message is clear. The Indian promoter exited long ago. The Japanese promoter keeps doubling down on India.

Look at the cars on the road today. The branding emphasis is on the giant "S" logo. 10-15years back, cars started selling with only “S” logo, 1st on premium nexa cars, then on all the models. You will hardly see Maruti branded cars on road now

For many younger buyers, the brand recall is shifting from "Maruti Suzuki" to simply "Suzuki". The transition is subtle but visible.

India is now the crown jewel of Suzuki Motor Corp. A substantial portion of Suzuki valuation come from Indian listed entity. Maruti $38bn mcap translate to $21bn (for 58% stake, $15bn if applied 30% Holdco disc).

Even beyond that, Maruti pays over $500m to Suzuki as royalty, that value must be over $5bn in the SoTP of Suzuki motors. Suzuki motors also have successful 2w biz in India, they are 6th largest 2w in India, clocking over 1lac units every month

In many ways, investors buying Suzuki Motor Corp are indirectly buying the India story. Cars sold by Suzuki in India is higher than overall car sold by Suzuki in other 100 countries combined

A rebranding to "Suzuki India" could also help shed the old "cheap small-car company" perception. As premium SUVs, hybrids & future EVs gain share, a stronger global MNC identity may command a different customer mindset.

Ownership, capital allocation, manufacturing integration, branding & growth strategy all point in one direction: this is increasingly Suzuki's India story.

Conclusion: Maruti only stays in Co. name hence should be renamed now
